subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, the review rubric, Data Security, Suspense/Streaming, Caching the Read Path, Common Anti-Patterns, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current React/Next.js App Router practice (RSC payload, server-only DTOs, React.cache, use() Promise handoff, Cache Components / 'use cache' / PPR, CVE-2025-55182).

cases.scenario: A dashboard page renders a header, a non-interactive metrics grid fed by a DB query, and one filter dropdown with a click handler. The developer has marked the entire page.tsx file 'use client' so the dropdown's useState works.
cases.context: Next.js App Router. The metrics grid and header have no interactivity; bundle size and TTI are a concern.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the component tree?
expected_flags: Marking the whole page 'use client' loses all RSC benefit — ships the whole page as a client bundle and re-runs on hydration
Move 'use client' to the thinnest interactive leaf (the dropdown), keep header/metrics-grid/layout as Server Components
Keep the DB query in a Server Component; pass server-rendered content (the grid) into the interactive shell via children/slot
Default is Server; a component is Client only because a forcing requirement forced it
expected_fix_hints: Extract the dropdown into its own small 'use client' component
Pass the Server-rendered grid as a children/slot prop to the interactive filter shell
absent_signals: Do not keep the whole page as a Client Component
Do not move the DB query into a Client Component / useEffect

cases.scenario: A Server Component does `const user = await db.user.findUnique(...)` and renders `<ProfileCard user={user} />`, a Client Component that displays only the name and avatar. The row also contains passwordHash, stripeCustomerId, and an internalRiskScore.
cases.context: Next.js App Router with a Postgres DB. Security review flagged the page.
cases.question: What is the vulnerability and how should the agent fix it?
expected_flags: Every prop passed to a Client Component is serialized into the RSC payload and shipped to the browser, including fields never rendered
passwordHash / stripeCustomerId / internalRiskScore are now visible in browser devtools — a data leak
Filter to a minimal DTO before crossing: return only { name, avatarUrl }
Centralize in a server-only Data Access Layer that authorizes and returns DTOs; back with the server-only package and/or taint APIs
expected_fix_hints: Map the row to a UI-shaped DTO in a 'server-only' module before passing it
Re-check authorization (resource ownership), not just authentication, in the DAL
absent_signals: Do not pass the whole DB row to the Client Component
Do not assume 'it's a Server Component so the props are private'

cases.scenario: A page Server Component awaits a 2s analytics query, then renders a child that awaits an independent 1.5s orders query, then renders the whole result. The page shows nothing for ~3.5s.
cases.context: Both queries are independent. The team wants the shell and header to appear immediately.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the data fetching and reveal timing?
expected_flags: This is a sequential waterfall — the orders query cannot start until the analytics await resolves, even though they are independent
Render the two reads as siblings (or Promise.all) so their awaits happen in parallel
Wrap each slow section in its own Suspense boundary co-located with the data so the shell/header flush immediately and each section streams in when ready
Dedupe any shared read with React.cache() / fetch auto-dedup
expected_fix_hints: Split analytics and orders into sibling Server Components, each in its own <Suspense fallback>
Use Promise.all only when one component genuinely needs both results
absent_signals: Do not keep the parent-await-then-child-await waterfall
Do not put one giant Suspense boundary at the page root

Recommends this expected fix or action: Use Promise.all only when one component genuinely needs both results.

cases.scenario: Under Cache Components (cacheComponents: true), a developer adds 'use cache' to a layout component that reads cookies() to greet the logged-in user, to 'make it fast'. In dev it errors / serves the wrong user's name.
cases.context: Next.js 16 App Router with Cache Components enabled.
cases.question: What is wrong and what is the correct caching design?
expected_flags: A component that reads cookies()/headers()/searchParams is request-specific (dynamic) and must NOT be cached — caching freezes one user's data and serves it to everyone
Cache only request-independent output; place 'use cache' close to the data (a cacheable function/component), not a whole layout that reads request input
Wrap the per-request greeting in Suspense and leave it uncached/dynamic (Partial Prerendering: static shell + dynamic holes)
Read cookies() in the leaf that needs it, not in the root layout, so the rest stays prerenderable
expected_fix_hints: Remove 'use cache' from the request-specific layout; cache the request-independent parts instead
Move the cookies() read down into a Suspense-wrapped dynamic leaf
absent_signals: Do not cache a component that reads cookies/headers/searchParams
Do not read request inputs high in the tree just to cache the layout

Surfaces this expected flag: Wrap the per-request greeting in Suspense and leave it uncached/dynamic (Partial Prerendering: static shell + dynamic holes).
Surfaces this expected flag: Read cookies() in the leaf that needs it, not in the root layout, so the rest stays prerenderable.

cases.scenario: An admin page reads `searchParams` and does `if (searchParams.role === 'admin') return <AdminPanel data={await getAllUsers()} />`. The developer also accesses params synchronously without await.
cases.context: Next.js 15+ App Router; params/searchParams are async.
cases.question: How should the agent review this Server Component?
expected_flags: searchParams is user-controlled URL input and is NOT an authorization signal — ?role=admin proves nothing
Re-verify the real session server-side and check authorization (does this user own/permit this resource), not just authentication
params and searchParams are async in the current App Router and must be awaited
Reading request inputs makes the subtree dynamic — read low in the tree, not in a shared ancestor
expected_fix_hints: Gate AdminPanel on a verified session role from the data layer, not on a URL param
await params / await searchParams before use
absent_signals: Do not trust searchParams/params/headers as a permission check

cases.context: The team conflates 'anything on the server' with this skill.
cases.question: How should the agent scope these requests?
expected_flags: The 'use server' mutation/action + revalidation trigger is out of scope — that is server-actions-design (the write path)
The SSG-vs-SSR strategy choice is out of scope — that is rendering-models
This skill owns the read-path RSC design; it can hand off the write-path and the rendering-strategy decisions to the owning skills
Correctly redirects rather than designing the mutation flow or picking a rendering strategy out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Route the mutation/revalidation work to server-actions-design
Route the SSG/SSR decision to rendering-models
absent_signals: Do not design the Server Action mutation flow here
Do not pick SSG vs SSR here

cases.scenario: An interactive chart (a Client Component) currently fetches its data in a useEffect on mount, causing a hydration delay and a double-fetch. The chart needs interactivity (zoom, tooltips).
cases.context: Next.js App Router, React 19. The team wants the data fetched on the server but the chart to stay interactive.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the data flow?
expected_flags: useEffect-fetch-on-mount produces hydration delay, double-fetch, and lost streaming benefit
Start the query in a Server Component and pass the unawaited Promise as a prop; unwrap it in the Client chart with use() under a Suspense boundary
The Promise must be created on the server, never freshly in the Client Component's render (otherwise it re-suspends forever)
The Suspense boundary must sit above the component calling use()
expected_fix_hints: Create the data Promise in the Server Component (or a cached server-only read) and pass it down
use(dataPromise) inside the 'use client' chart, wrapped in <Suspense fallback>
absent_signals: Do not keep fetching in useEffect on mount
Do not create the Promise inside the Client Component's render
